summary:
I re-checked the external facts the final report will state, using about 75 fresh WebSearch calls. WebFetch and curl were blocked for nearly every finance and government site, including bofip, IBKR, CME, CFTC, barchart, jpx and hkex, so the evidence comes from search snippets. Each fact below has a verdict and a source URL. Full table (42 rows): cv_fonds_fisc/facts_verified.csv. Sensitivity re-run of the critic's Monte Carlo: cv_fonds_fisc/mc_rate_tax_sensitivity.csv.

Corrections that change what the report says:
1. **Form 3916 penalty.** The fine of 5 % of the balance when accounts reach €50k or more must not be stated. The Conseil constitutionnel struck it down (QPC 2016-554, 22 Jul 2016) and it was replaced by an 80 % surcharge on tax evaded (art. 1729-0 A). What remains: €1,500 per undeclared account per year (€10,000 for a non-cooperative state) and a 10-year limitation period. Bitcoin held on a foreign exchange goes on form 3916-bis: €750 per account, €1,500 if worth more than €50k.
2. **ECB rate dispute resolved.** The deposit rate is 2.50 % since 16 Sep 2026: a 25 bp hike decided 10 Sep, after 2.00 → 2.25 % on 11 Jun. The Banco de España "unchanged in September" page is about 2025. €STR was 2.19 % on 9 Sep; after the hike it is about 2.43 %, inferred from the spread rather than sourced directly. The next meeting is 29 Oct, with about a 60 % market probability of 2.75 %. The critic's 2.3 % is about 0.13 pt too low. Re-run with its own seed:
   - DIY v5, 10-year median after-tax CAGR: 1.43 / 2.43 / 3.16 % at USD 100k / 250k / 1M (was 1.33 / 2.33 / 3.04).
   - iMGP DBi ETF route: 3.47 % (was 3.37).
   - Probability of a nominal loss over 10 years: 41 / 36 / 32 %.
3. **BNC scenario now quantified.** Requalification under art. 92-2-5° (criteria from CE Boniface 2001: number and frequency of trades, technicality, diversity of contracts, portfolio size, profit size) means the progressive income-tax scale plus social levies. Losses then offset only same-nature BNC profits, in the same year and the next 6 years (not 10), and never QQQ gains. Median after-tax CAGR falls to:
   - 0.72 / 1.60 / 2.18 % at a 30 % marginal rate;
   - 0.23 / 1.03 / 1.56 % at a 41 % marginal rate.
4. **iMGP DBi share classes were mislabelled earlier.**
   - R USD = LU2951555585: Euronext Paris DBMF, share class launched 7 Mar 2025, Xetra since 2 Feb 2026, also on the LSE.
   - LU2951555403 = R EUR unhedged, ticker DBMFE.
   - R EUR HP = LU3359622902 (MFEH): launched 13 May 2026, Xetra 18 May 2026, Euronext Paris 21 Sep 2026 (confirmed).
   - All three: TER 0.75 % and accumulating. AUM USD 698M at 18 Sep 2026.
   - The fund replicates the SG CTA index (all CTA styles), so it is not a pure trend system. "Europe's only managed-futures UCITS ETF" is false.
5. **BNP Paribas Easy Managed Futures UCITS ETF:** LU3307218399, launched 29 May 2026, TER 0.60 %, accumulating. It runs an in-house trend model, euro-hedged, via swaps built with BNP Global Markets. Xetra ticker EEAU since 24 Jun 2026; AUM about €10M. A Paris ticker was not confirmed.
6. **Other funds:**
   - Man AHL Trend Alternative retail class DNY (LU0424370004) costs about 2.75 % a year (2 % management plus a performance fee), not 1.72 %.
   - The Winton I EUR ISIN is IE00BG382R37 (1.05 % ongoing charges).
   - AQR Managed Futures UCITS: A USD class LU1103257975 charges 0.60 % plus 10 % performance fee; retail RAE class LU1662502183 has a 1.39 % TER. It is not an ETF.
   - Man Active Trend UCITS ETF was only registered with the Central Bank of Ireland on 2 Jul 2026; no listing yet.
   - None of these is PEA-eligible.
   - No insurer could be confirmed offering any of them inside an assurance-vie.
7. **Missing trend run in the backtest.** It stops on 2026-07-10. The SG CTA index was +8.6 % YTD at that date, +11.1 % by 31 Aug (local data) and +15.9 % YTD around 18 Sep 2026 (best year since 2022).
8. **KIDs by exchange.** HKEX does publish an EEA futures KID, which contradicts the IBKR/Darwinex claim that it does not. SGX and ASX have no KID, so SGX iron ore, FTSE Taiwan, Nifty and ASX contracts are likely blocked for French retail clients. CME KIDs exist for the micro grains (updated 9 Feb 2026).
9. **MJY history.** CME delisted the micro yen contract in March 2022 and relaunched it on 26 Feb 2024.

Confirmed as stated:
- PFU 31.4 % (12.8 % income tax + 18.6 % social levies, LFSS 2026, loi 2025-1403, art. 12). It applies to capital gains from the 2025 income year and to interest and dividends from 1 Jan 2026. Assurance-vie, PEL/CEL, rental income and property gains stay at 17.2 %. The 2027 budget bill (filed 30 Sep 2026) may extend the higher rate to assurance-vie.
- Art. 150 ter: every sale or settlement is taxable, so each roll realises P&L. Profits go under the PFU. Losses offset same-nature gains, QQQ included, over 10 years.
- An accumulating UCITS ETF is taxed only when sold.
- IBKR: blocks futures without a KID for EEA retail clients; pays no interest on commodity-segment cash, so the futures margin earns 0 (excess cash can be swept to the securities segment); pays benchmark − 0.5 %, nothing on the first USD 10k, and a pro-rata rate below USD 100k NAV.
- Fed funds 3.75–4.00 % after the 16 Sep 2026 hike.

Liquidity of the micro contracts:
- **Liquid:** 1OZ (record 115k contracts a day in Jan 2026), OSE Nikkei 225 Micro (0.64M a day in FY2025), FDXS (28k a day in 2026), M6E (about 19k a day).
- **Moderate:** M6A (about 3.9k a day, open interest 4.8k), MNG.
- **Thin:** FSXE (2.4k a day, about €13M), M6B (about 580 a day, open interest 1.5k).
- **Unverified, likely thin:** MZC, MZW, MZS and MJY — no 2026 volume or open-interest data found. Micro corn's tick (0.5 ¢ on 500 bu) is twice standard corn's in relative terms.

Remaining gaps:
- The post-hike €STR level is not directly sourced.
- The assurance-vie listings and the BNP Paris ticker are unconfirmed.
- Micro grains and MJY have no 2026 volume or open-interest figures; check them in TWS.
- The 2778-SD monthly deadline was not re-verified.
